content.essentialTips:
Best Time to Visit: December to April for dry season, avoid hurricane season (June-November)

  • Currency: Trinidad and Tobago Dollar (TTD) - US dollars widely accepted
  • Language: English (official), but you'll hear lots of local slang and expressions
  • Tipping: 10-15% at restaurants, round up for taxi drivers
  • Internet: WiFi available in most hotels and cafes, consider getting a local SIM card
content.budgetPlanning:
Daily Budget Estimates:

  • Budget: $50-80 USD per day
  • Mid-range: $80-150 USD per day
  • Luxury: $150+ USD per day

Money-Saving Tips:

  • Eat at local "doubles" stands for cheap, authentic meals
  • Use public transportation (maxi taxis) instead of private taxis
  • Visit free beaches like Maracas Bay instead of paid resort beaches
  • Shop at local markets for souvenirs instead of tourist shops
content.foodDining:
Must-Try Local Dishes:

  • Doubles: Fried bread with curried chickpeas - the national street food
  • Bake and Shark: Fried shark in fried bread with condiments
  • Pelau: One-pot rice dish with meat and vegetables
  • Roti: Flatbread with curry fillings
  • Callaloo: Leafy green soup, often served with crab

Dining Tips:

  • Street food is generally safe and delicious
  • Try local hot sauce - but start small, it's spicy!
  • Restaurants typically open around 11 AM and close early
content.transportation:
Getting Around:

  • Maxi Taxis: Shared minivans, cheapest option for longer distances
  • Route Taxis: Shared cars following set routes
  • Private Taxis: More expensive but convenient, negotiate price upfront
  • Rental Cars: Available but traffic in Port of Spain can be challenging

Inter-Island Travel:

  • CAL (Caribbean Airlines): Flights between Trinidad and Tobago
  • Ferry: Cheaper option, scenic route, takes about 2.5 hours

Transportation Tips:

  • Traffic can be heavy during rush hours (7-9 AM, 4-6 PM)
  • Always confirm taxi fares before getting in
  • Maxi taxis don't run late at night
content.accommodation:
Accommodation Types:

  • Hotels: Range from budget to luxury, concentrated in Port of Spain and Scarborough
  • Guesthouses: More affordable, family-run options
  • Vacation Rentals: Great for longer stays, especially in Tobago
  • All-Inclusive Resorts: Mainly in Tobago, good for beach vacations

Booking Tips:

  • Book early during Carnival season (February/March)
  • Tobago has more beach resort options than Trinidad
  • Consider staying near public transportation routes
  • AC is essential - check that it's included and working
content.safetyHealth:
Safety Precautions:

  • Avoid walking alone at night, especially in Port of Spain
  • Don't display expensive jewelry or electronics
  • Use hotel safes for valuables
  • Be cautious with beach vendors - polite but firm "no thank you"
  • Stick to well-populated areas and established beaches

Health Tips:

  • Vaccinations: Routine vaccines up to date, consider Hepatitis A/B
  • Water: Tap water is generally safe, but bottled water is readily available
  • Sun Protection: Strong tropical sun - use high SPF sunscreen
  • Mosquitoes: Use repellent, especially during rainy season

Emergency Numbers:

  • Police: 999
  • Fire/Ambulance: 990
  • Tourist Hotline: 868-623-1932
